24 The diagram shows an experiment to produce a stationary wave in an air column. A tuning fork,
placed above the column, vibrates and produces a sound wave. The length of the air column can
be varied by altering the volume of the water in the tube.
tuning fork
air column
water
tap
The tube is filled and then water is allowed to run out of it. The first two stationary waves occur
when the air column lengths are 0.14 m and 0.42 m.
What is the wavelength of the sound wave?
A
0.14 m
B
0.28 m
C
0.42 m
D
0.56 m

hints: Notice the air column is open at the tuning fork and closed by water, so there is an antinode at the top and a node at the water surface.
Recall the closed-pipe resonance lengths $L = \lambda/4, 3\lambda/4, 5\lambda/4...$ for the 0.14 m and 0.42 m positions.
Subtract the two given lengths $0.42 \text{ m} - 0.14 \text{ m}$ and relate that $0.28 \text{ m}$ gap to a fraction of $\lambda$.
walkthrough: Identify the pipe: open top above the air column and closed bottom at the water gives a node at water and an antinode near the open end.
State the rule for a closed pipe: $L = (2n-1)\lambda/4$. The shortest length $L_1 = 0.14 \text{ m} = \lambda/4$.
The next resonance as water runs out is $L_2 = 0.42 \text{ m} = 3\lambda/4$.
Subtract to eliminate end effects: $L_2 - L_1 = 3\lambda/4 - \lambda/4 = \lambda/2$.
Substitute values with units: $\lambda/2 = 0.42 \text{ m} - 0.14 \text{ m} = 0.28 \text{ m}$.
Solve: $\lambda = 2 \times 0.28 \text{ m} = 0.56 \text{ m}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: 0.14 m is the first resonance length, which is only one quarter of a wavelength for a pipe closed at the water surface.

B.explanation: 0.28 m is the increase in length $0.42 - 0.14$, which equals half a wavelength, not the full wavelength.

C.explanation: 0.42 m is the second resonance length, which is three quarters of a wavelength, not one full wavelength.

D.explanation: The length difference $0.28 \text{ m}$ is $\lambda/2$, so $\lambda = 0.56 \text{ m}$.
